titulo: One news item in several varieties
intro: Compare three fictional versions of the same local news item and notice regional vocabulary and forms of address.
p.variedad.consejo: Spanish has many varieties. It is written with v and sounds like b: «ba-rye-DAD».
p.ustedes.consejo: It does not always indicate respect. In the Americas it is also used among friends and family.
p.vosotros.consejo: It has its own forms: «vosotros habéis». In the Americas it is hardly used.
p.autobús.consejo: It is the most general word. In Mexico you also hear «camión» and in Argentina, «colectivo».
p.línea.consejo: You say «la línea 5». It has a tilde on the í: «LI-ne-a».
p.colectivo.consejo: In Argentina «el colectivo» is the city bus. In other countries it means something else.
p.parada.consejo: It comes from «parar». You say «la parada de autobús». It is feminine.
p.ayuntamiento.consejo: The y of «ayuntamiento» sounds as in «yo»: «a-yun-ta-MYEN-to». It is widely used in local news.
p.aviso.consejo: It is written with v and sounds b. You say «un aviso» and «dar aviso».
p.ruta.consejo: It is almost a synonym of «línea». The initial r sounds strong: «RRU-ta».
b1.texto:
Many speakers in Spain use **vosotros** for an informal group; **ustedes** is usual across much of the Americas and also appears in parts of Spain. **Vos** is used in several American regions, with forms that vary. Bus vocabulary also varies: **autobús**, **camión** and **colectivo** are used in different places, but usage can differ by city and context.

The examples below are fictional and show broad clues, not rules for every speaker or country.
b2.f0.texto: The town council has opened a new bus route today.
b2.f1.texto: Here they opened a new bus route today.
b2.f2.texto: In my city they inaugurated a bus route.
b2.f3.texto: Have you all seen the notice at the stop?
b2.f4.texto: We already tried it this morning.
b2.f6.texto: The stop is next to the market.
b2.f7.texto: The new bus passes through my neighbourhood.
b4.texto:
**Address.** The same message changes with the group you speak to.

- **Madrid**: *¿Vosotros habéis visto el aviso?*
- **Mexico City**: *¿Ustedes ya la probaron?*
- **Buenos Aires**: *¿Vos ya la probaste?*

**Past of today.** In the Madrid version, **ha abierto** presents the news as close to the present. In the other two the indefinido is used (**abrieron**, **inauguraron**) to tell what happened today. It is a regional preference, not a rule for everyone.

**Vocabulary.** *Línea*, *ruta* and *colectivo* name a transport route; *autobús* is the most general word.
b4.e0.texto: The new bus stops next to the bus stop.
b4.e1.texto: You all already tried it this morning.
b4.e2.texto: The neighbours wait for the bus on the corner.
b5.titulo: The stop next to the market
b5.f0.texto: The market wakes up before the whole city.
b5.f1.texto: The fruit crates pile up next to the empty stop.
b5.f2.texto: A cold light slides down the roof of the shelter.
b5.f3.texto: A stray dog sniffs the wet ground patiently.
b5.f4.texto: Behind the houses, the sky turns pale pink.
b5.f5.texto: The new bus appears at the end of the avenue with its headlights on.
b5.f6.texto: An elderly woman raises her hand and smiles at the driver.
b5.f7.texto: The doors open with a sigh of air and rubber.
b5.f8.texto: Inside it smells of fresh paint and freshly made coffee.
b5.f9.texto: Through the window, the morning passes slowly like a quiet film.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That is it: «vosotros» is the usual plural in Spain.
b6.o1.refuerzo: There «ustedes» is used for the plural.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Well done: with «ustedes» the third person plural is used.
b7.pregunta: Complete with the form that goes with «ustedes».
b8.o0.refuerzo: The market is only next to the stop.
b8.o1.refuerzo: A cancellation would be the opposite of a new service.
b8.o2.refuerzo: That is it: all three speak of a new bus route.
b8.pregunta: What new service do all three describe?
b9.frase: Los tres textos hablan de una nueva línea
b9.traduccion: The three texts talk about a new route
b10.o0: Muestran patrones regionales, no una regla para todos
b10.o0.refuerzo: That is it: they are regional variants, all valid.
b10.o1: Solo las formas de Madrid son correctas
b10.o1.refuerzo: No: the examples are variants, all valid.
b10.o2: Todos los países de América usan vos
b10.pregunta: Which statement best describes the examples?
b11.pregunta: Write how «autobús» is said in Buenos Aires.
p.abrieron.consejo: From «abrir», to open. The «v» is not here, but «ie» forms a diphthong «bryé».
p.inauguraron.consejo: From «inaugurar», to open officially. The «au» is a diphthong, read as one sound.
p.probamos.consejo: From «probar», to try. The «-amos» ending is the past for «nosotros».
p.probaste.consejo: From «probar». The «-aste» ending is the past for «tú», and with «vos» it is «probaste» too.
p.apilan.consejo: From «pila», a pile. The «-an» ending is for «ellos» or «ellas».
p.marquesina.consejo: From «marquesa», a canopy. The «-ina» at the end names a shelter, like at a bus stop.
p.callejero.consejo: From «calle», street. A «perro callejero» is a dog that lives on the street.
p.olfatea.consejo: From «olfato», sense of smell. Dogs «olfatean» to find things with their nose.
p.tiñe.consejo: From «teñir», to dye or tint. The «ñ» is pronounced like «ny» in «canyon».
p.faros.consejo: Plural of «faro». It also means lighthouse, but for cars it means headlights.
p.encendidos.consejo: From «encender», to switch on. The masculine plural agrees with «faros».
p.goma.consejo: Rubber, like the material of tyres or an eraser. The «g» before «o» is hard.
p.transporte.consejo: From «transportar», to carry. The stress falls on «POR», the second syllable.
p.textos.consejo: Plural of «texto». The «x» sounds «ks», as in «texto».
p.muestran.consejo: From «mostrar», to show. The «ue» forms a diphthong, read «we».
p.patrones.consejo: Plural of «patrón», pattern or model. The stress falls on «TRO».
p.regionales.consejo: From «región», region. The «io» is a diphthong, and the «g» before «i» sounds like «h».
